rule.summary: Nasdaq-100 weights by listed market value, not free-float market value. Since 1 May 2026 a stock whose free float is 33.3% or less is counted at the lesser of its listed market value or three times its free-float value. Above 33.3% float the full listed value counts. Float is only re-measured at the quarterly reviews (March, June, September, December), using data as of the last trading day of the prior month; future lock-up expiries are not anticipated.

proforma.method: Pro-forma at constant 10 Nov 2026 prices with the rest of the index unchanged. On 10 Nov, fully counted mega-caps carried about 1.667% of the Nasdaq-100 per $1 trillion of market value (Apple 8.47% / $5.06T, Nvidia 6.78% / $4.07T, Microsoft 6.60% / $3.96T, Amazon 4.87% / $2.93T). SpaceX’s 2.82% therefore counts about $1.69T of its $1.94T total market value (about 87%). If Nasdaq’s 30 Nov float measure is above 33.3%, all $1.94T counts: about 3.22%. If Nasdaq uses a float near FloatCap’s 4.33B shares (31.9%), the cap is 3 × 31.9% = 95.6% of value: about 3.08%. After that, further unlocks do not raise the weight; only price moves do.

inputsSource.label: QYLD holdings weights and Nasdaq market caps, 10 Nov 2026 (compiled by BestFirms)

caveats: Nasdaq does not publish the float or index share count it uses for SpaceX, so the counted share of value (about 87%) is implied from ETF weights, not reported.
The 21 Dec review uses float as of the 30 Nov close. The 8 Dec unlock is after that date, so it could only be counted from the March 2027 review.
Musk’s 366-day release (14 Jun 2027) and other insiders’ shares are not free float under Nasdaq’s rules, so the bars exclude Musk’s 4.77B shares.
Undated extended lock-up releases (after Q4 2026, Q1 and Q2 2027 results) are left out of the bars.
Index caps (24% single stock; 4.5% / 48% aggregate rule) are not binding for SpaceX at these weights.
